items.evidence: Draft: 'deferred (about 1.3k)'; after Jeff's 2026-10-13 05:00Z 'no Python in release builds' it became required (~2k). The app swap to the C++ transmitter landed as 2b6d29b at 06:31Z.

items.evidence: (nn*(num % period)) % period wraps when den > ~380k with large or negative n0; mix_turns wraps for a period past ~3e9 (e.g. f_hz=-0.1 at fs=250); normal slots have n0 < 1.5e7.

items.what: ce.phase_at is discontinuous at every whole-symbol tau, because the pulse is cut at +-8 symbols with a nonzero step. Chunking a very long pass off-grid therefore changes the audio. No preset reaches this.
items.evidence: Step p(8)=0.006; jumps up to 0.0199 rad (0.003-0.005 rad at tau 1000/5000). Off-grid chunking differs by up to 7.4e-3 at amplitude 0.5 over 602 samples. Needs a piece starting more than 16,384,005 samples (~2048 s; exact threshold 2048.000625 s) after t0.

items.what: ce.cw_phase_turns with a NaN tau subtracts every window through searchsorted. The C++ records this as a deviation and does not copy it.
items.evidence: port:ce_tx notes.

notes:
Sources: the five workflow journals (map wf_361c7c27-ab5, wave 1 wf_d27e26c8-142, wave 2 wf_bd73eb47-f31, wave 3 wf_8af3e0e3-a7f, rerun wf_5c80865c-1d3), their scripts, and port_plan.md.

How the review-bug counts were made:
- bugs_found_in_review counts findings marked fixed=true, so it includes a few test gaps and doc fixes.
- Wave 1 is 46 fixed (precoder_morse 6, polar_header 6, frame 13, filters 8, infra 13) out of 60 findings in all.
- Wave 2 is 12 fixed (picture_chain 5, one of them a test gap; ce_tx 5; l_tx 2).
- Stage 1 completion is about 13 real fixes: pass_audio 2 plus a doc fix, codec_cli 6, and the final review 5 of its 7 fixed=true, the other two being 'checked correct'.

Wave notes:

waves.what: Receiver foundations. A skeleton step and its review came first: rx constants generator, types/pyjson/trackbase (PathFn, ChanCapture), shared math (npstats, linalg, bspline) and the rx_types.hpp/_rx.py converters. Three lanes followed, each with its own review: frontend (frontend, rules, chan, StreamFE, math/convolve, npcomplex), math (special, ndfilter, cubic_spline, npfft, acquire_stats) and demod (demod, ldemod, render planes, ce_rx, lwave_rx).

Ported track.py's tracker core (track, Kalman/RTS, refine_timing) and its timing and verification code (fit_timing as a direct sparse gather, gate V, refine_path/line_path). Also ported acquisition A1/A2 (carrier lines, preamble search, lead_in_span) and A3 (track_before_detect) plus cwid. Each part was reviewed, and every parity file carries a whole-caller A/B.

items.what: scipy 1.18.1's make_lsq_spline returns finite but wrong coefficients when early data points are sparse before a gap, because its qr_reduce skips rows with offset[i] > i. PathFn only checks that the coefficients are finite, so it silently uses the wrong spline as the frequency path; the port reproduces this bit-exactly.
items.evidence: Least-squares residual is 10^2 to 10^5 times the optimum in 1324 of 2000 targeted random trials (scratchpad sweep). The guard is the finite check in sstvae/qrss/track.py PathFn. A residual check, or dropping knots that have no data, would catch it in both implementations.

items.what: np.linalg.eigh returns NaN for NaN input without raising, so the tracker's `except LinAlgError` fallbacks never fire on that path and the NaN propagates.
items.evidence: measured: np.linalg.eigh(np.array([[nan,0],[0,1]])) returns NaN with no exception

items.what: PathFn([nan]) raises ValueError, and two or more NaN times, or all times zero, raise LinAlgError from polyfit. Neither is caught, so a detection with a bad path takes down the caller instead of being skipped.
items.evidence: PathFn([nan]) gives 'cannot convert float NaN to integer'; the NaN-times and zero-times cases give 'SVD did not converge'. Pinned in native/tests/qrss/test_trackbase.cpp test_pathfn refusals; inferred from sstvae/qrss/track.py.

items.what: PathFn.__init__ never checks that len(f) == len(w) == len(t): it indexes f and w by argsort(t), so a longer f or w is silently truncated and a shorter one raises an IndexError naming an internal index.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/track.py:255-259 (skeleton review); no current caller trips it

items.what: With repeated times the reference PathFn is not reproducible across hosts. np.argsort's default kind is unstable, and numpy 2.x dispatches it to x86-simd-sort kernels by CPU feature, so the order of equal times and the spline coefficients can differ between AVX-512 and non-AVX-512 machines.
items.evidence: inferred from code (track.py:258 np.argsort(t)); measured ~5e-12 coefficient differences against the stable C++ order

items.what: blank() of 1 to 100 FE samples raises ValueError 'array of sample points is empty' instead of passing through. With hop=200, running_median's centres are empty for n <= 100, so a capture of up to 25 ms crashes the blanker.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/frontend.py running_median (centres = np.arange(hop // 2, max(n, 1), hop)) and _interp_to_samples; tests/test_qrss_native_frontend.py::test_blank_refuses_what_the_reference_does pins it for n in (1, 50, 100); the C++ keeps the behaviour

items.what: A negative `chunk` makes `range(0, n, chunk)` empty, and four functions then return without raising: running_median, normalise and _interp_to_samples (frontend) and acquire.spectrogram return their uninitialised np.empty buffers, while ce.matched_filter and lwave.matched_filter return all zeros. Separately, acquire.spectrogram raises "object of type 'numpy.int64' has no len()" for a 0-d starts.
items.evidence: inferred from code: frontend.py chunk loops over np.empty outputs; acquire.py:246-258; ce.py:483-500, lwave.py:367; tests/test_qrss_native_ce_rx.py test_matched_filter_chunks_and_positions. chunk=0 raises from range(). Nothing passes a chunk today.

items.what: _noise_response, _fold_power and _fe_power are lru_cached but return writeable arrays, unlike _fe_flat and _fe_response. A caller that modifies one in place silently corrupts the cache for every later noise_psd call with the same arguments.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/frontend.py:293-337 (no writeable=False) against :351 and :364 (writeable=False)

items.what: scipy.ndimage.median_filter's 1-D fast path reads one element past the array when the window is exactly 2n+1 (lim2 == 0). Tie-breaking, and NaN results, then depend on whatever memory follows the array; the receiver cannot reach this.
items.evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_ndfilter.py::test_nan_follows_scipy failed for (n=2, w=5) before that case was excluded: [nan, nan] from scipy vs [nan, 0.659] from its own generic path. Unreachable because spectral_shape clamps w to at most n_bins, so lim2 > 0.

items.what: Given an explicit n, np.fft.irfft(empty, n) reads x[0] past the end of the input and returns garbage instead of raising. The port refuses.
items.evidence: numpy 2.5.3 _pocketfft_umath.cpp irfft_loop copies x[0] unconditionally; without n numpy raises 'Invalid number of FFT data points (-2)'; native/core/math/npfft.cpp irfft_impl refuses

items.what: For a strong preamble, gammaincc underflows to 0 at every scale and np.argmin ties to scale 0 (g=1, the fully noncoherent statistic). preamble_search then refines df/tau on that surface whatever scale carries the signal; the 'p underflows' branch picks the cell by lam2 but not the scale. Wave 5 found that ordinary strong signals reach this branch.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/acquire.py:852-857. Wave 4 math: a planted ctest cell with Lambda about 800 at all four scales gives p = 0 and best = 0. Wave 5 A1/A2 review: A2 Lambda saturates at about 620 for CE from about 0 dB SNR, and pmin < 1e-250 at 0 and 10 dB (probe2.py); the C++ takes the same branch.

items.what: demod.extract and ldemod.extract_l mutate their argument by setting track.m = np.asarray(m). EM re-extraction relies on this, but extracting twice with different m from one TrackResult leaves the second m behind; the binding reproduces the mutation.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/demod.py:245-246, ldemod.py:326-327; test_extract_with_given_m_replaces_the_tracks; replace_m in demod_rx.hpp

items.what: frame.spread_signs checks only the shape of hdr_bits, although its error text says 'values of 0/1'. Bits of 2 silently give a sign of -3, so a header-decode bug producing non-binary bits would corrupt round B's spread subtraction with no error; frame.assemble does validate values.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/frame.py:302-308 against :338; probe: hdr_bits=2*kb gives values from ldemod.data_estimates_l

items.what: Given an L spec, ce.mean_template, _mean_template_grid, phase_at and at_positions have no waveform guard. They fail deep in frame.layout with a misleading assertion about header slots.
items.evidence: The assertion reads "1237 header slots for 2474 bits". sstvae/qrss/ce.py:124-128 and frame.py:271-280. The receiver never calls them this way.

items.what: The reference is inconsistently strict about track field types. CE demod.symbol_estimates indexes tr.m/u/P/N/psi directly, so a list raises TypeError, while ldemod.symbol_estimates_l wraps every field in np.asarray, so a list works.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/demod.py:71-73 against ldemod.py:158-159; matters only for hand-built stubs

items.what: known_symbols did not check the header bits' length. A short header silently returned a _Known whose pos and val differ in length, while make_classes on the same input raises.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/track.py:454-463; probe: known_symbols(SHORT, bits[:-1]) -> pos (3574,), val (3573,). Fixed in wave 7 (commit ce73aff: known_symbols takes its values from make_classes and refuses a short header with make_classes' error).

items.what: derotate(chan, fn) with an fn that returns a scalar, such as a constant frequency, fails inside np.interp instead of broadcasting. Only array-valued paths work.
items.evidence: np.interp raises 'fp and xp are not of the same length.'. sstvae/qrss/track.py:303-313: a scalar g gives a cumsum of length 1, then np.interp runs over n indices. Every current caller passes a PathFn.

items.what: refine_timing's 3-D (gamma) Newton branch is never taken by any fixture or simulated pass, so it is untested in the reference as well as the port.
items.evidence: measured: MEDIUM at -6 dB with tx_ppm -30: branch evaluated on 3 tracks, never taken (zk(th3) > zk(th) + 1 never holds). Injected gamma 3/-6: not taken. 12/25/-40: None on both sides.

items.what: verify's blind path computed the coarse timing grid twice on the same z_d and path: once inside verify_track (n_best 1) and again for the runners-up (n_best=V_TIMING_TRIES). Sharing the fit roughly halves the blind gate's cost on a weak candidate.
items.evidence: In sstvae/qrss/track.py verify(), the verify_track(... fit=fit) call is followed by fit_timing(..., n_best=V_TIMING_TRIES) with the same fn and z_d. Fixed in wave 7 (commit ce73aff, _fit_timing_tries: one grid for both, covering verify and verify_l).

items.what: verify keeps the first base's Z_ref with `if best is None or alt.z_ref > best.z_ref`. If that first Z_ref is NaN, every later comparison is False, so _flat_path and line_path can never be chosen; the C++ copies this.
items.evidence: inferred from code, sstvae/qrss/track.py verify (base loop); latent: an all-erased frame gives 0.0, not NaN

items.what: _segment_timing's single-segment fallback fits with the outer `delta`, not the loop's `d_`. This is harmless today, but anyone who reorders that walk will hit it.
items.evidence: inferred from code, sstvae/qrss/track.py _segment_timing; d_ only diverges after the ptp >= 300 ppm refusal, which never reaches the single-segment fit (branch coverage via scratchpad lines.py tracer)

items.what: fit_timing's two correlation paths (FFT when nlag > 64, direct otherwise) disagree at the capture's end: one zero-extends an interpolation pair that straddles len(x), the other drops it. Only receiver.channel_for's padding hides this, so an unpadded capture, for example from a future live path, would get a timing that depends on the search width.
items.evidence: inferred from code plus probe: test_probe_fit_timing_random local searches on both sides of the 64-lag switch agree only on padded captures

items.what: _cell_line indexes stat[d0, b] first and indexes the requested drift d only if it survives the straight-drift comparison. An out-of-range d with a low v therefore succeeds, and whether a bad drift index is noticed depends on the statistic's value.
items.evidence: A._cell_line(cs, 0, 13, 10.0) succeeds; inferred from sstvae/qrss/acquire.py _cell_line

items.what: Some return types depend on the value. CarrierCandidate.f_hz is np.float64 when refined from a cell but a Python float when hint_line falls back to the hint, and _phase_line's slope is np.float64 only when fitted.
items.evidence: inferred from sstvae/qrss/acquire.py hint_line/_phase_line; the binding mirrors it (cell_to_py)

items.what: _phase_line divides by sxx without a guard. A degenerate input (all chunks at one time, or zero weight spread) emits a RuntimeWarning and returns a NaN slope.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/acquire.py:823 RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in scalar divide' during test_fine_sums_coherent_phase_line

items.what: track_before_detect with a band narrower than its clip span returns a confident hit at the wrong frequency. np.clip is called with a_min > a_max, the negative slice bounds wrap, and bins are read from the wrong end of the grid. The port author called this the serious one of the three A3 bugs; the C++ refuses with NotImplementedError.
items.evidence: Probe: band (1000, 1060), candidate 1030 Hz -> hit centre 1020 Hz, path 1046.5-1050.75 Hz (sstvae/qrss/acquire.py, the band clip in track_before_detect/l_pilot_bins)

items.what: tbd_viterbi with B < |max_step| < 2B (B bins) fails with an opaque numpy broadcast ValueError instead of a parameter error. With |max_step| >= 2B it silently behaves differently, so the valid step range is undocumented and unchecked.
items.evidence: Probe of tbd_viterbi with an 81-bin E and max_step 100 -> ValueError 'operands could not be broadcast together'

items.what: _path_line on a path with fewer than 2 points raises UnboundLocalError, because the refit branch references a variable assigned only inside the loop. A degenerate path that reaches TbdHit.f_hz crashes instead of giving NaN or a clear error.
items.evidence: Probe: A._path_line(FreqPath with 1 point) -> UnboundLocalError; mirrored as acquire::UnboundLocal and pinned in test_acquire_tbd.cpp

items.what: numpy 2.5's complex arithmetic is its own loop formulas, chosen by CPU dispatch. Multiply is FMA-fused only on the X86_V3/V4 targets, complex/real division is Smith's method (multiply by the reciprocal), and complex np.abs is a SIMD hypot, larger*sqrt(fma(r,r,1)), not libm's. The reference's bits therefore depend on the host CPU; npcomplex.hpp reproduces the V3/V4 forms with std::fma on every machine.
items.evidence: The textbook forms disagree with numpy in about 25% (multiply), 43% (division) and 35% (abs) of results (npcomplex.hpp, numpy 2.5.3). With NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES down to X86_V2, 44% of the complex products changed (frontend review). This Xeon dispatches X86_V4. blank, normalise, channelise, extract and the matched filters are bit-equal only with these forms. On a non-AVX-512/FMA host the 1-ulp/99.9% bar, not bit equality, is the operative check (demod review).

items.what: Python's builtin abs() of an np.complex128 scalar is numpy scalar math (npy_cabs, i.e. libm hypot), not the np.abs ufunc formula. Mapping every abs() of a numpy complex to the ufunc formula is wrong wherever the reference applies the builtin to a scalar from np.sum.
items.evidence: measured: 4224 of 20000 random complex sums differ by 1 ulp between the np.abs formula and builtin abs; std::hypot vs builtin abs 0/50000 (wave 5 A1/A2 review; fix at native/core/qrss/acquire_a12.cpp lead_in_impl)

items.what: numpy 2.x vendors the same pocketfft as native/third_party, so numpy FFTs agree bitwise; scipy's FFTs are ducc0. Complex-complex convolutions come out bit-identical, but when one operand is real scipy transforms it with ducc0's real-input FFT, which pocketfft-style code cannot reproduce to the bit. Statistics downstream of such a convolution must be specified to rounding.
items.evidence: noise_psd worst rel 0 under both rules over 90 frequencies. oaconvolve worst 5.9e-16 (frontend port), and 1.1e-15 relative over many-batch sizes up to 400k x 2001 (review, test_convolve_many_blocks). ~21% of lead-in MF samples bit-equal, 6e-16 relative; a pocketfft probe matched at n=1250 but not at power-of-2 lengths (wave 5 A1/A2 review). Vendored pocketfft is bit-identical to numpy 2.5.3's for every length 1..65536 incl. Bluestein primes (test_qrss_native_npfft.py::test_c2c_every_length).

items.what: numpy 2.5 does not run complex64/float32 FFTs uniformly in single precision. Forward fft/rfft compute in double and round once (fct is the Python int 1, which only the double loop accepts), while ifft/irfft run pocketfft's float plans; the release notes claim all four are native single precision. em.py:501 calls np.fft.fft on a complex64 R and needs the complex64 overloads.
items.evidence: pfu.fft.resolve_dtypes((complex64, int, None)) -> complex128 loop; a float-plan port mismatched 192/200 random length-4 transforms, while widen/compute/narrow matched; test_npfft single-precision digest 32b785ca...

items.what: scipy.signal.oaconvolve runs its FFTs in single precision on a complex64 input even with float64 taps, so track._lowpass's result depends on its input dtype. track and fit_timing pass complex128 z_d, so the receiver is unaffected.
items.evidence: scratchpad lp.py: complex64 rows 1.2e-7..1.7e-7 vs 1e-15 for complex128/float64

items.what: numpy's float32 np.log is its own SIMD algorithm (AVX2/AVX512F), not correctly rounded and not logf: about 5% of float32 arguments differ by 1 ulp. A1's parabola vertex and A3's tbd_emissions/_bins_path depend on it, so it was ported as math/nplog.hpp log_f32, which is exact on every non-negative float32. numpy's float64 log on AVX-512 is SVML and differs from glibc too.
items.evidence: np.log(np.float32(7)) = 0x1.f2272cp+0 vs correctly rounded 0x1.f2272ap+0 (wave 4 math). test_numpys_float32_log; exhaustive probe found 0 mismatches over 0x0..0x80000000 plus negative ranges, and the test keeps [0.5,2) (8.4M values, ~2 s) (wave 5 A1/A2 review). float64 log differs on about 0.37% of inputs in (0,1) and 0.012% overall (wave 5 A3/cwid review).

items.what: numpy's SIMD/AVX-512 np.exp, and SVML expm1, are about 1 ulp from glibc on ~5% of arguments. Anything downstream is therefore a tolerance claim rather than bitwise: mean_template's exp(-v/2), gumbel_p and hence TbdHit.p_value, and track's templates sf.
items.evidence: mean_template worst 1.57e-16, ~95% bit-identical, 100% with nu = 0 (wave 4 demod). gumbel_p at most 4e-16 relative, measured 2.0e-16; TbdHit.p_value 1.6e-16 (wave 4 math review) and 2.1e-16 (wave 5 A3). templates sf 1.9e-10 elementwise (wave 5 track). data_estimates' exp(-beta^2 rho/2) happens to agree for the rho in use (0, 0.054).
items.where: ce_rx mean_template, acquire_stats gumbel_p, track templates

items.what: np.angle is a SIMD arctan2, 1 ulp from std::atan2 in about 7% of arguments. It is the main source of A2's phase and tau0 differences, far under the bars.
items.evidence: smoke diff: phase worst 3.5e-12 rad, tau0_s worst 4.0e-14 s

items.what: Squaring an np.float64 scalar (x ** 2) calls libm pow, which differs from x*x on about 1 in 1200 values; squaring an array is exact. GCC folds pow(x, 2.0) into x*x, so the port keeps pow with a volatile exponent.
items.evidence: Measured in the wave 4 math lane. Applied to CubicSpline's dxr[0]**2 and dxr[-1]**2 (native/core/math/cubic_spline.cpp scalar_square), a1_gamma's rho and demod::np::py_pow; pow(x, 2.0) equals x*x for K_LIN, A0, 0.5 and 0.8 (demod review).

items.what: CPython 3.12+'s sum() uses Neumaier compensation only on its exact-float fast path (PyFloat_CheckExact). Summing np.float64 items takes the plain '+' path, so faithfully copying the compensated sum is wrong; the first draft of demod's combine did that.
items.evidence: inferred from CPython bltinmodule.c builtin_sum_impl; demod.cpp combine() is now a plain sum (demod.calibrate / ldemod._combine sum(1.0/v ...))

items.what: np.maximum(-0.0, 0.0) returns +0.0 and keeps NaN, so std::max and std::fmax are both wrong for render.g_shrink's max0. The port uses isnan(w) ? w : (w > 0 ? w : 0.0).
items.evidence: native/core/qrss/render.cpp; test_render.cpp pins the bit pattern of g_shrink(-0.0)

items.what: np.polyfit/np.linalg.lstsq are accurate only normwise, so a small slope beside a large intercept is not elementwise-reproducible across SVD implementations. On ill-conditioned weighted line fits numpy is the less accurate side, so PathFn line tolerances must be sized for numpy's error.
items.evidence: Skeleton port: normwise 3.1e-15, and PathFn evaluation 9.3e-12 Hz worst. Review: with two points 1 s apart and one weight at the 1e-9 floor, numpy's slope is off by 3.9e-8 vs exact rationals and the Jacobi-SVD port's by 6e-12, a 3.9e-6 Hz disagreement extrapolated 100 s (probes p4/p6; trial 41 of p2: 8.6e-9 Hz scalar diff).
items.where: native/core/math/npstats polyfit, linalg lstsq; trackbase PathFn

items.what: OpenBLAS's dscal by 1/NaN leaves exact zeros as zero (it short-circuits on x == 0), so numpy's solve gives a partly finite answer for a NaN pivot. A portable LU gives all NaN, so do not pin NaN patterns from numpy's solve or inv.
items.evidence: np.linalg.solve([[nan,1],[0,1]],[1,1]) -> [nan, 1.]; port -> [nan, nan]

items.what: np.convolve, np.dot and np.vdot go through numpy's DOUBLE_dot -> cblas (OpenBLAS DYNAMIC_ARCH), so their summation order is the CPU's BLAS kernel and cannot be bit-exact portably. This affects track._smooth, cwid.match and track/ltrack's alpha/delta, and the timing fit's lstsq residual threshold can flip an outlier decision at the boundary. The C++ sums _smooth sequentially (1e-16) and emulates the SkylakeX ddot for match, which is bit-exact only on that dispatch.
items.evidence: np.convolve order by kernel length: plain for n<=8, sequential FMA for n of 12 and 15, SIMD for n>=16; the tracker uses n=32 and 99 (L: 16 and 49). 'same' with 15 taps goes through ddot, not small_correlate (up to 11 taps). SkylakeX ddot: FMA, four 8-lane accumulators in blocks of 32 folded to 4 lanes, four 4-lane accumulators in blocks of 16, combine ((a0+a1)+a2)+a3 then (s0+s2)+(s1+s3), FMA scalar tail; dot_order.py 0 mismatches in 2000 trials at n=176,16,32,40,100,7; match 0 difference over 5000 draws. Call sites inferred from track.py:620-631, 970, 1670; ltrack.py:908, 925, 1109-1120.

items.what: numpy reductions depend on memory layout, not only values. preamble_scales sums pairwise when the chunk axis is innermost and one term at a time otherwise, and _preamble_sums' einsum output is Fortran-ordered. Likewise s.sum(axis=0) is a row-by-row running sum for C-order stacks but pairwise per column for F-order or transposed ones, so a port that copies to C order (pybind11 c_style|forcecast) matches only the first case.
items.evidence: Real _preamble_sums S (strides (16, 336, 420336)): 10910/8283/6524 of 26271 cells differed for k=1/10/2 and 0 for k=5; np.ascontiguousarray(S) gave 0; up to 42% of cells overall (wave 4 math review). F-order and .T stacks of 9/17/40/200 rows differ from the sequential sum, while every row-major layout is equal (wave 5 A3/cwid review, probe_strides.py).

items.what: On numpy 2.5, np.einsum('fcs,tcs->ftc', optimize=True) is not c_einsum: it routes through bmm_einsum to a BLAS zgemm per chunk. _preamble_sums' S therefore depends on the BLAS build and CPU and comes back Fortran-ordered, so any golden vector built from S is BLAS-dependent.
items.evidence: measured S max-rel 1e-15..2e-15 vs per-cell sequential sum; S.flags F_CONTIGUOUS in the reference; 2-3.5% of S elements bit-equal (review); Lambda rtol < 1e-9 with identical cells

items.what: Python 3.13 evaluates -2j*np.pi as complex(+0.0, -2pi), applying the unary minus to the complex literal first. This sets the sign of zero in exp() phasors when matching numpy to the bit.
items.evidence: inferred while porting the A2 templates' phasor construction; pinned by the template digests

items.what: np.add.reduce starts from the identity +0.0, so np.sum([-0.0]) is +0.0. A C++ sum must be seeded with 0.0, not with the first element.
items.evidence: inferred from numpy source and checked bit-exactly by shape_z / smooth probes (wave 5 A3/cwid review)

items.what: The reference tracker's Kalman/RTS pass is badly conditioned. Its diffuse initial velocity covariance (0.1 Pu) cancels down to about q*Pu and keeps ~7 digits, so a 1-ulp change in Pu_g (BLAS ddot in _smooth) or one ulp of SIMD exp in templates' sf moves P by up to 2.0e-5 relative. The same Python on another CPU/BLAS disagrees with itself at that level, so u/P can only be held conditionally, and the task's 1e-10 bar was unreachable.
items.evidence: explore_kf2.py: 'Pu_g + 1 ulp: P rel 8.4e-07'. Lead-in TINY gate-V run: P 2.0e-5, u 2.7e-9, pu 8.9e-8. CE TINY gate-V run: P 8.4e-7, u 6.7e-10. FULL pass: u 9.6e-10, P 6e-8. With the C++ _smooth and templates swapped in: 0 on all 7 calls.

items.what: Gate V's Z_ref is ill-conditioned in the reference itself: about 1e-8 relative on a signal and 5e-5 on noise, and worse when the Kalman q sits at the grid floor. Every original scenario had q at grid index 1-2, so later ports that compare Z_ref (A3, live gates) need bars of about 1e-5 at the floor.
items.evidence: Port: handed the C++ timing (1e-12 samples away), the reference's Z_ref moves 2.2e-8 (drift), 1.4e-8 (TINY -12) and 6.3e-5 (noise, 0.75926 to 0.75921). Review: at Q_GRID[0] = 8.6e-10, a 1e-13-sample change of tau0 moves Z_ref 5e-7 to 1.1e-6 and P about 1e-4. test_probe_steady_weak_q_floor: own nudge z_ref 7.81e-7, P 8.36e-5; C++ vs reference z_ref 3.65e-7, P 4.62e-5. Weak steady signals land at the floor (sim -15 dB seed 11, -17 dB seed 10).

items.what: templates' sf = MF{a^2 (1 - exp(-v))} loses relative accuracy where v is small, turning one ulp of exp(-v) into 1.9e-10 relative in sf. Using np.expm1 would make it well-conditioned; this Python change was not made.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/track.py:771; test_templates worst sf 1.93e-10 elementwise, <1e-14 of scale

items.what: To get symbol_mf bit for bit, the C++ emulates numpy's x86 einsum SSE2 sum (two lanes, blocks of 8, unfused muladd). numpy's NEON muladd is fused, so on aarch64 the parity tests may see ulp differences in symbol_mf that are not a port bug.
items.evidence: inferred from code: native/core/qrss/track.cpp around line 178 (einsum emulation comment) and numpy's simd muladd definitions; worth re-measuring on linux-aarch64 or macos-arm64

items.what: np.hanning and libm cos agree bitwise on this x86-64 glibc machine, so _carrier_lines is asserted bitwise. If a macOS or Windows parity run ever fails there, suspect the window before the peak search.
items.evidence: test_carrier_lines bitwise on all scenarios + 16 random captures (x86-64 glibc)

items.what: cwid _ln_i0 agrees with the reference to 1e-14 for x >= 1 but only to about 5e-11 relative near 0, so its parity test needs a split tolerance. The port and the review blame different causes: the port blames scipy's i0e vs the C++ series, the review numpy's SVML float64 log, where log(i0e(x)) + x cancels at small x.
items.evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_cwid.py ln_i0 test, measured worst 5.3e-11 near 0 (port); test_ln_i0_and_combine (review). window_llr stays bit-identical because it is cast to float32.

items.what: The ctest digests for SHORT with spread depend on std::exp(-0.01728) through data_estimates. The exact value lies 0.118 ulp from its double, so any libm with error under 0.88 ulp rounds the same way: safe, but fragile.
items.evidence: inferred from code: native/tests/qrss/test_demod.cpp test_short_spread, demod::np::py_pow

items.what: ce.phase_at casts NaN or out-of-range tau to int64. numpy does this with a RuntimeWarning, but the C++ static_cast is undefined behaviour; the two agree on x86-64 only because both compile to cvttsd2si (INT64_MIN).
items.evidence: test_probe_mean_template_presets (NaN, +-inf and 1e300 tau): identical non-finite pattern; the cast sits in ce.hpp (transmit lane), not changed later

items.what: The CE matched filter multiplies every tap in the window, including zero taps and samples clipped to z's ends, by z[clip(idx)]. A NaN or inf at z[0] or z[-1] therefore spreads as NaN*0 to every position whose window runs off that end, and an optimisation that skipped zero taps would break parity.
items.evidence: native/core/qrss/ce_rx.cpp mf_impl; probe cases 'z with NaN at the clipped edge' and 'z with inf, complex' are byte-equal

items.what: For the noise scenario's flat 3-point FreqPath (10 s knots over -10..1800 s), z_d differs by 1.6e-10 relative between the C++ and scipy PathFn fits. The dense paths from refine_path agree bitwise.
items.evidence: noise track z_d 1.61e-10 against track z_d 0 (QRSS_PARITY_WORST run)

items.what: The skeleton's PathFn and median run faster than numpy through the binding.
items.evidence: Through the pybind11 binding, conversion included: PathFn fit of 4000 points over 1800 s 4.4 ms vs Python 9.0 ms; evaluating 20000 points 1.05 ms vs 1.40 ms; np.median of 100001 float32 1.06 ms vs 1.41 ms (measured on 4 shared CPUs).

items.what: Without -mfma, std::fma is a library call per operation, and numpy's fused complex multiply needs two. freqz's Horner loop and oaconvolve's spectral product now run an AVX2+FMA target clone chosen at run time with __builtin_cpu_supports, giving the same bits on both paths.
items.evidence: _fe_power went from about 3x slower than numpy to 1.7 ms against Python's 5.4 ms (native/core/math/convolve.cpp mul_spectra / horner dispatch; timing measured before compaction)

items.what: Building oaconvolve's whole rows x n buffers at once made the C++ 2x slower than scipy. Processing about 54 blocks at a time gives the same bits much faster.
items.evidence: 3400 x 2420 complex buffers, about 130 MB each: 0.85 s against scipy's 0.36-0.39 s, although pocketfft's batched transform alone matches ducc0 (0.083 s vs 0.094 s). Batched: 0.50 s including binding copies (timing2.py: before 0.829-0.850 s, after 0.501 s). FULL-slot audio_to_fe is then 0.61 s against Python's 0.68 s.

items.what: Front end on a FULL slot (920 s): everything is faster in C++ except normalise, where numpy's AVX2 sort of 512x400 blocks beats the sliding-window median. The port and the review report different Python times for audio_to_fe.
items.evidence: Port (min of 3): audio_to_fe 0.61 s vs Python 0.68 s; channelise 0.17-0.21 vs 0.32-0.34 s; blank 0.62 vs 1.15 s; normalise 0.47-0.49 vs 0.26-0.49 s (load-dependent). running_median over 92,000 windows of 400 samples is ~4 us/window with a sorted sliding window (nth_element: 0.54 s; C++ 100 ms/10 ms 0.369 s, 1 s/50 ms 0.509 s). Review (4 shared CPUs), Python vs C++: audio_to_fe 3.05 vs 0.69 s; channelise 1.38 vs 0.21 s; running_median 1.07 vs 0.53 s; blank 1.03-1.59 vs 0.86-0.88 s; oaconvolve 5M x 121 1.30 vs 0.31 s; normalise 0.27-0.45 vs 0.42-0.64 s.

items.what: The math lane's special functions and median filter run at scipy's speed, as expected from a port of the same C. The real win is the spectrogram, which reuses one buffer with fft_inplace; preamble_p is slower in C++.
items.evidence: Native (RelWithDebInfo -O2, including pybind conversion) vs scipy/numpy, min of 5 (timing_math.py): spectrogram 73 frames x 9601 bins at fs 4000 25.2 vs 41.1 ms (1.63x); cfar_normalise 21.8 vs 24.3 ms; spectral_shape 11.6 vs 12.3 ms; median_filter n=9601 w=161 0.50 vs 0.62 ms, w=321 0.58 vs 0.53 ms; gammaincc k=10 on 21x400 0.85 vs 0.80 ms; gammainccinv over 300 A1 shapes 0.24 vs 0.22 ms; CubicSpline n=5161 build 0.71 vs 0.67 ms, evaluate 660 points 0.026 vs 0.031 ms; preamble_p (21,73,10) 1.51 vs 1.28 ms and (21,400,10) 8.7 vs 7.1 ms; one 16000-point fft 0.211 vs 0.205 ms.

items.what: The 2-D fft binding first went through fft_rows' vector API (np.asarray, a vector copy, a transform buffer, a copy into the result) and ran 3x slower than numpy. Copying each row into the result and calling fft_inplace there closed most of the gap.
items.evidence: 150 x 16000: 93-97 ms vs numpy 29-30 ms before, 36-39 ms after (timing_rows.py, commit 775e51f); the remaining gap is -O2 vs numpy's -O3 pocketfft and forcecast

items.what: Under --native-qrss=rx the acquire suite ran only slightly faster than on Python, so the claimed 2.5x does not hold. FFTs and medians dominate and run in C on both sides; the C++ wins mostly on spectrogram framing.
items.evidence: tests/test_qrss_acquire.py -m 'not slow': 20.6 s native vs 22.4 s Python; FULL spectrogram 0.39 s vs 0.50 s; cfar 0.353 s vs 0.380 s; gammaincc on 150k points 11.7 ms vs 11.5 ms

items.what: extract/extract_l gain little, because the work is gathers plus a hypot per element (np.abs must match bit for bit) plus vector allocation, which numpy already does near memory speed. Either way it costs about 10 ms per 30-minute pass.
items.evidence: FULL pass, 50600 latents, genie track, best of 5 (port), Python vs native: CE joint 14.4 vs 8.0 ms (1.8x); CE plain 14.2 vs 7.9 ms; L joint 8.8 vs 5.7 ms (1.6x); L plain 7.9 vs 5.3 ms. Review (full stub, AVX-512): extract full 34.9 vs 21.3 ms (x1.6), short 2.7 vs 1.5 ms (x1.8); extract_l l-full 16.3 vs 8.7 ms (x1.9), l-short 1.8 vs 0.8 ms (x2.3); block_estimate 4.35 vs 1.23 ms (x3.5).

items.what: np::index, numpy's negative-index and bounds rule, cost a third of extract as an out-of-line call per gathered element. Inlining it with a [[noreturn]] cold thrower fixed this; every numpy-index-emulating gather should take that shape.
items.evidence: callgrind: np::index 39M Ir of ~98M per extract; native extract on the FULL stub went from 24.9 ms (Python 19.3 ms) to 13.2 ms; native/core/qrss/demod.hpp index()/index_error()

items.what: The receive-side kernels are 1.1x to 7.6x faster in C++. _mean_template_grid gains least because exact phase arithmetic and exp dominate it.
items.evidence: Port, FULL at 250 Hz: ce.matched_filter 160.9 vs 46.5 ms (3.5x); lwave.matched_filter 236.1 vs 45.8 ms (5.2x); _mean_template_grid 55.2 vs 50.9 ms; decoder_planes 8.4 vs 5.1 ms. Review, best of 3: ce.matched_filter FULL complex 190 vs 48.5 ms (x3.9), real 123 vs 16 ms (x7.6); lwave.matched_filter l-full 246 vs 46 ms (x5.3); mean_template FULL 623 vs 126 ms (x4.9); _mean_template_grid 55 vs 50 ms (x1.1); matched_filter call overhead for 3 positions 52.8 vs 8.7 us (x6).

items.what: track() and refine_timing are several times faster in C++ on the receiver's own calls.
items.evidence: Port: FULL pass track total 19.6 s -> 3.67 s (5.3x; per call 2.41/8.64/8.55 s vs 0.36/1.58/1.74 s); SHORT 0.39/1.04/1.18 s vs 0.04/0.18/0.23 s (5-10x); TINY 0.12/0.31 vs 0.01/0.06 s; refine_timing FULL 0.8767 s -> 0.2230 s (3.9x), SHORT ~3x. Review (4 shared Xeon CPUs): symbol_mf over a FULL grid 0.07-0.20 vs 0.31-0.94 s; track per call SHORT 0.18-0.36 vs 1.1-1.7 s, MEDIUM 0.10-0.50 vs 0.95-2.55 s, TINY 0.05 vs 0.30 s; refine_timing MEDIUM 0.05-0.28 vs 0.29-1.04 s; l-short receive_pass with the rows 1.71 vs 3.46 s; test_qrss_smoke 3.9 vs 7.4 s, test_qrss_ltrack 3.5 vs 6.1 s, test_qrss_lreceiver 2.5 vs 3.2 s.

items.what: fit_timing ported as a direct sparse gather confirms plan 2b's 10-20x claim for long frames; on short frames the speed-up is mostly overhead. The gather is cheap because a run of lags within one binade shares a rounding offset, so it becomes contiguous and vectorises (AVX2 target clone, same bits).
items.evidence: Port: blind n_best=8, FULL -12 dB Python 13.98 s vs C++ 1.40 s; SHORT -6 dB 0.31 vs 0.11 s; one FULL grid 0.22-0.28 s (0.29 ns per term); fit_statistic x4 0.25 s. Run-based gather took a FULL grid from 0.5 s to 0.22-0.28 s; lag/delta blocking was slower (3.12 s vs 2.26 s per FULL fit); an AVX-512 clone gave no measurable gain. Review: FULL n_best=8 Python 13.74 vs C++ 1.52 s (9.0x); one grid Python FFT 2.99 s vs 0.225 s (13.3x); SHORT 0.32 vs 0.15 s (2.1x), one grid 0.04 vs 0.009 s (4.1x). FULL nlag 1255, 147 rows, nfft 524288.

items.what: verify_track (blind fit plus the withheld track) is about 9x faster on FULL and 4.5x on SHORT.
items.evidence: FULL -12: Python 16.88 s, C++ 1.85 s. SHORT -6: Python 0.63 s, C++ 0.14 s. verify on SHORT 0.27 s vs 0.67 s; on TINY 0.09 s vs 0.22 s.

items.what: A1/A2 in C++ is at or slightly ahead of Python end to end, but the preamble sums and preamble_p lose to numpy. numpy does S as a BLAS zgemm, and the build is baseline SSE2 with FMA forbidden by parity. These are the levers if A2 costs too much on Android.
items.evidence: Port, best of 5: A1 on a 600 s capture 11.9 vs 8.7 ms (x1.4). preamble_search per candidate from FE: CE 53.9 vs 43.4 ms (x1.2), L 59.1 vs 40.7 ms (x1.5); from a precomputed _A2Input CE 30.6 vs 39.3 ms, L 28.7 vs 29.0 ms. C++ CE breakdown: a2_input 7.2, a2_mf 0.55, preamble_sums 17.6, preamble_p 26 ms. Via binding: _a2_input CE 16.8 -> 6.9 ms, L 18.8 -> 11.2 ms; lead_in_span CE 7.9 -> 3.6 ms, L 12.6 -> 7.4 ms. S: numpy 5.5-8.6 ms vs C++ 12.7-20.4 ms; restructuring as a per-(c,f,q) correlation with a 4-way unrolled MAC cut it from 29.6 to ~18 ms with no order change. preamble_p gammaincc 26 ms vs scipy 17.5 ms. Review, best of 7, Python vs C++: _preamble_sums CE 0.0172 vs 0.0220 s, L 0.0079 vs 0.0131 s; _a2_mf 0.0013 vs 0.0006; A1 FULL 0.011 vs 0.008; preamble_search CE 0.048 vs 0.045, L 0.050 vs 0.041; lead_in_span CE 0.008 vs 0.004, L 0.013 vs 0.007.

items.what: For the whole live-only joint acquire() with only the acquire_stats rows applied, the C++ was slower than Python because of preamble_p. With the A1/A2 rows added it is faster; A3, still Python at that point, dominates.
items.evidence: CE SHORT: Python 1.286 s; acquire_stats rows only 1.49 s; stats + acquire_a12 rows 1.118 s (scratchpad time_acq.py)

items.what: A FULL-slot track_before_detect is 3-6x faster in C++ at half the peak memory. Python's biggest single cost was TbdHit.f_hz recomputing np.polyfit inside the dedup loop.
items.evidence: Port: 896 frames, all_hits: Python 2.12 s / +202 MB vs C++ 0.68 s / +100 MB; with shape (FULL, L_FULL) 4.44 s vs 0.78 s; cProfile: 3816 polyfit calls = 0.97 s of 2.99 s (acquire.py:1282 and :1080). Review: 1.97, 4.54 and 2.3 s Python vs 0.64, 0.86 and 0.64 s C++ for a single CE spec, the joint shape test and the L spec; +202 MB vs +100 MB.

items.what: cwid.read_ml is 50-90x faster in C++. In Python the margin pass, a second constrained DP per character, dominates.
items.evidence: 2x176 LLR stack: margin=True 24.2 ms vs 0.27 ms (90x); margin=False 5.67 ms vs 0.112 ms (50x)

items.what: Python's mutable ChanCapture._psd became a NoisePsdSlot: a shared_ptr behind a mutex with get_or_compute, shared by copies. It computes once under contention, with no mutable global.
items.evidence: native/tests/qrss/test_trackbase.cpp test_psd_slot: computed == 1 under 8 threads

items.what: np.average(weights=) is used by the acquire, track and ltrack lanes, which would each have re-derived it. The skeleton review added it once as math::average, bit-exact with numpy's TypeError/ZeroDivisionError texts.
items.evidence: acquire.py:820-821, track.py:621/627, ltrack.py:1110/1116; native/core/math/npstats

items.what: The NoisePsdFn seam lets chan.cpp (and later lead_in_span) call frontend::noise_psd directly in C++. The rows still honour a test's monkeypatched frontend.noise_psd, keeping argument spies working without a Python round trip on the normal path.
items.evidence: tests/qrss_native/chan.py _noise_psd(); tests/test_qrss_native_chan.py::test_the_seam_gets_the_references_arguments

items.what: scipy's not-a-knot CubicSpline solve goes through solve_banded and LAPACK zgtsv with complex right-hand sides, but the matrix is real, so a small zgtsv emulation is bit-exact with no LAPACK dependency. The vendored pocketfft also matches numpy's bit for bit.
items.evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_cubic_spline.py::test_bitwise (n up to 2000); tests/test_qrss_native_npfft.py::test_c2c_every_length

items.what: M*M in a1_gamma can be computed in double instead of int64: Python's exact product rounded once equals the double product for every |M| < 2^53. This removes signed-overflow UB with no change in bits.
items.evidence: ctest pins a1_gamma(3037000500) = (0x1.56fbe7c0f11bap+31, 0x1.0e38e38e24c69p+0), the Python value

items.what: Python writes the inverse-variance kappa combination twice, inline in demod.calibrate and as ldemod._combine, and the two are identical. The C++ has one demod::combine, and _combine's row is an alias.
items.evidence: sstvae/qrss/demod.py:178-191 vs ldemod.py:210-222

items.what: In both implementations extract recomputes median(|u|^2 over pos >= 0) over the whole grid in each of its four symbol_estimates calls. Computing it once per track would remove most of extract's remaining cost without changing any result.
items.evidence: demod.py:73; about 4 x 29k-element nth_element on a FULL pass; C++ extract on a full stub 21.3 ms (Python 34.9 ms), symbol_estimates(ref) alone 2.15 ms, slower than Python's 1.72 ms

items.what: track._parabola duplicates acquire._parabola, and ltrack imports it. The C++ keeps one parabola (float and double overloads) in acquire_stats, and the track_timing rows map _parabola to it.
items.evidence: wave 4 math notes; wave 5 track timing notes: rows file maps _parabola to acquire_stats._parabola (float32 dispatch for ltrack's L pilot)

items.what: Caching TbdHit.f_hz per hit is a one-line Python fix worth about a third of track_before_detect's runtime, with no format change. The C++ caches it with identical output.
items.evidence: cProfile: 3816 polyfit calls = 0.97 s of 2.99 s on FULL. Fixed in the reference in wave 7 (commit ce73aff: @functools.cached_property, 'TbdHit.f_hz fitted once').

items.what: acquire::np_log_f32 in the A3 lane and math::np::log_f32 (nplog.hpp) in the A1/A2 lane were two transcriptions of numpy's simd_log_FLOAT. The A3 copy was deleted at merge.
items.evidence: native/core/qrss/acquire_tbd.cpp vs wf_c19e1b62-a4e-2/native/core/math/nplog.hpp (A3/cwid review); merged in commit 21ba9bf 'wave 5 follow-ups (one float32 log ...)'

items.what: lstsq/polyfit use a one-sided Jacobi SVD, eigh a cyclic Jacobi eigen-solver, and solve/inv partial-pivot LU, because native/ has no LAPACK. They agree with numpy to rounding (normwise), not bitwise.
items.evidence: lstsq x within 1e-10 and singular values within 1e-12; solve/inv/eigh/eigvalsh 1e-12 (~1e-15 well-conditioned); eigenvector signs not compared. Rank decisions are bit-exact, including rcond <= 0 / >= 1. For [[nan,1],[0,1]]x=[1,1], solve gives [nan,nan] where numpy gives [nan,1]. eigh with non-finite input returns NaN, like numpy, and raises nothing.

items.what: PathFn sorts with std::stable_sort (NaN last), refuses f/w of a different length from t, and emits no RankWarning. A NativePathFn called on a scalar returns np.float64 where the reference's spline path gives a 0-d ndarray, and the text of scipy's make_lsq_spline 'Out of bounds' refusal is approximated.
items.evidence: Repeated times give ~5e-12 spline-coefficient differences (tie order); distinct times are bit-exact (572 cases, 0 differences; a 4000-point 1800 s path max diff 0.0). The length refusal reads ValueError 'PathFn: t, f and w must have the same length'; every receiver call site passes equal lengths.

items.what: PassResult.load requires the dtypes the receiver writes and maps missing/extra meta keys differently from Python. Other narrow I/O differences: a Python int in a float field is written '0.0', not '0'; a 0x0 cov is written (0,0); JSON ints are limited to int64; bindings narrow float64 arrays to float32; and save maps RuntimeError to OSError.
items.evidence: Required dtypes: float32 z/w/hdr_llr/psi, complex64 ch, 2-D float64 timing_cov. An extra meta sub-key is ignored where Python raises TypeError; a missing one gives KeyError where Python gives TypeError. Receiver-produced files are byte-identical in both directions across 10 variants (one pinned at sha 575b8255..., 2544 bytes), and the meta JSON is identical to json.dumps.

items.what: pass_uid's binding takes f_hz as a double; Python given an np.float32 multiplies by 1000 in float32 before round(). Past 2^63 the C++ prints with printf('%.0f').
items.evidence: Exact on glibc/macOS and UCRT from VS 2019 16.2; older MSVC runtimes would print zeros after 17 digits (unreachable for a real frequency). The receiver always passes a Python float.

items.what: noise_psd takes an explicit NoisePsdOptions::old_edge_noise; left unset, it reads QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE as the reference does. rules::set_old writes only the C environment, and the Python binding writes os.environ first so os.environ, monkeypatch and getenv agree.
items.evidence: rules::old/set_old race through getenv/setenv, as documented: set the rules at startup or pass old_edge_noise. old, set_old and apply agree with os.environ in one process and in a child; refusal texts are identical.

items.what: Python's lru_caches became mutex-guarded LRU caches of immutable shared_ptr<const> results. Unlike the reference, _noise_response, _fold_power and _fe_power cannot be mutated through a returned value.
items.evidence: lane notes: caches are mutex-guarded LRUs or function-local statics; noise_psd_at computes its table once with eight concurrent callers (ctest counting stub)

items.what: The front end changes only how work is batched, with outputs bit-equal. The bindings accept the chunk arguments and ignore them; running_median/normalise use a window kept sorted across hops; oaconvolve works in batches of about 2^17/n rows; StreamFE.push consumes its buffer from an offset.
items.evidence: chunk == 0 raises the reference's 'range() arg 3 must not be zero'. For chunk < 0 the reference returns uninitialised np.empty memory and the binding returns the real result. Medians are bit-equal and oaconvolve matches its earlier output and scipy bitwise. StreamFE's outputs, a0 and pending() equal live.StreamFE after every push.

items.what: Front-end edge refusals differ on absurd inputs. quantise_mix raises OverflowError for |f|*64 >= 2^63 (int64 Rational) where Python builds a huge Fraction, noise_psd with fs=0 does not raise ZeroDivisionError, and unported scipy modes and shapes raise NotImplementedError.
items.evidence: Unported: 'valid', N-D, scalar worN and other maximum_filter1d modes. make_chan returns a dict that the row converts with _rx.to_ref. convolve is bound only for the parity tests and substitutes nothing.

items.what: A 3-point CubicSpline matches only to 1e-13, because scipy solves it densely with LAPACK gesv. The native CubicSpline refuses real y (scipy's real path divides where its complex path multiplies by a reciprocal), other bc_types, extrapolate=False and multi-dimensional y.
items.evidence: 3-point: at most 1e-13 relative near the knots; unreachable from preamble_search, which always has hundreds of knots

items.what: median_filter with a window of exactly 2n+1 (scipy's lim2 == 0) uses scipy's generic NI_Select path, because the fast path reads past the array. The value always matches but the sign of a zero or a NaN case can differ; only odd sizes, mode reflect and 1-D are supported.
items.evidence: ndfilter parity: every n 1..40 against every odd window up to 2n+7 is bit-exact elsewhere; the 2n+1 window is value-exact only

items.what: npfft supports only norm='backward', 1-D input or a forward fft along the last axis of a 2-D array. It refuses irfft of an empty input with explicit n (ValueError 'irfft: empty input') where numpy reads past the buffer.
items.evidence: anything else raises NotImplementedError; longdouble FFTs not compared

items.what: Several acquire_stats edges differ from the reference. gumbel_p agrees only to 4e-16 on AVX-512, NEP 50 mixed typing for _parabola is emulated only in the binding, and some refusal texts and return types differ on unrealistic inputs.
items.evidence: gumbel_p: numpy's own exp and SVML expm1, so A3's p < pfa decision could flip only within an ulp of pfa. preamble_scales with a negative scale: own ValueError text instead of numpy's reshape error. Negative spectrogram chunk: NotImplementedError. py_round with 4*fs past int64: OverflowError. a1_gamma at fs < ~0.375 Hz returns np.float64 where Python returns Python floats (and ZeroDivisionError at M=0); left unchanged.

items.what: The demod bindings read track arrays through np.asarray, assume gi(p) = p - pos[0] instead of calling tr.gi, and refuse some argument forms with their own text. Non-0/1 hdr_bits are refused where the reference computes 1 - 2b.
items.evidence: Lists work where CE's reference raises TypeError. extract converts q to uint64 first ('q must fit in uint64'). The matched filters require a 1-D z and refuse a 2-D pos with ValueError (numpy reports a broadcast failure). A 0-d/2-D meas gives IndexError for size 0. meas and hdr_bits are converted eagerly. With several malformed arrays a different IndexError can come first. longdouble/object z computes in float64/complex128. kappa_estimates_l returns Python floats. g_shrink(+inf) gives NaN without numpy's RuntimeWarning.

items.what: Four non-bitwise seeds in the track core are accepted and pinned: _smooth sums sequentially where np.convolve uses OpenBLAS ddot, templates use libm exp instead of numpy's SIMD exp, _lowpass computes complex64 input in double, and refine_timing's Newton step uses the math lane's LU. The swap test shows _smooth and templates' sf are the only array-level seeds.
items.evidence: _smooth 1e-15/1e-16; templates c 1 ulp (3e-16 rel), sf 1.9e-10; _lowpass on complex64 1.6e-7 apart (real callers pass complex128). refine_timing within an ulp: tau0 1.4e-17, ppm 1.9e-16, cov 2e-18 relative. Matching _smooth exactly would tie the C++ to one CPU's BLAS kernel (SkylakeX vs Haswell vs NEON differ).

items.what: track()'s freq argument must be a PathFn (Python's or native), and a track with no timing raises the same AttributeError, only earlier. A few binding edges differ on exotic inputs.
items.evidence: Binding edges: select_q accepts lists (reference: AttributeError); remove_spread checks shape at a different point (both ValueError); z_ref_stat raises a different error type on malformed input. _recenter returns a C++ PathFn evaluating to 1e-9 Hz. symbol_mf's chunk is ignored. The pass_uid sha8 suffix may differ because it hashes float32 z. Non-1-D header bits now match numpy's outcomes and messages.

items.what: fit_timing correlates by the direct sparse gather for every lag count (plan 2b), where the reference switches to FFT correlation above 64 lags. The grids agree to rounding and every peak, decision and timing is the same; a term straddling an end of x counts 0, as in the reference's own direct path.
items.evidence: C++ grid vs reference FFT grid 1.05e-13 of scale (bar 1e-12); vs its direct path 4.4e-15; tau0 8.2e-12 CH samples, slip 5.0e-11; receiver.channel_for pads captures so the straddle never happens there

items.what: Gate V parity bars are set from the reference's own conditioning rather than the task's 1e-8. With identical inputs the glue is bit-exact (test_gate_v_composition).
items.evidence: Z_ref is held to 1e-7 (measured 4.5e-8) and resid_ratio to 1e-6 (measured 1.1e-7). On the noise capture: Z_ref 1e-4 absolute (6.1e-6), P 1e-3 (1.3e-4). At the q floor: Z_ref 1e-5 (3.65e-7), P 1e-3 (4.6e-5), u 1e-7 (4.3e-9).

items.what: Small track_timing differences: fit_statistic is not bit-exact (~1e-15, from _lowpass and the dense-MF oaconvolve), and a NaN-score peak sorts last where Python's -score key is unordered for NaN. Complex known symbols are refused, and verify returns a value copy whose identity the rows restore where Python returns its argument.
items.evidence: statistic x 9.8e-16 of scale, sig2 2.3e-15; identity is preserved for refine_path/line_path when unchanged and for verify_track's timing when fit=False

items.what: A2 matches only to rounding. S is a per-cell in-order sum where numpy's einsum uses BLAS zgemm, chunk phases use std::atan2 instead of numpy's SIMD arctan2, oaconvolve's FFT order differs, and lead_in_span's z comes from a convolution scipy does with ducc0's real-input FFT. The returned span can differ only if z lands within an ulp of z_min.
items.evidence: S ~2e-15; Lambda 1.4e-15 / 2.0e-15 (bar rtol 1e-9) with the same argmax cell every time; f_hz identical; tau0_s 4.0e-14 s; phase 3.5e-12 rad; m/local 6.5e-16 / 9.4e-16; lead-in z ~6e-16 with ~21% of samples bit-equal; preamble_p on a given S exact

items.what: carrier_lines breaks exact float32 ties highest bin first, where numpy's unstable argsort may order them differently. The A1/A2 binding also refuses some inputs, nests helpers that cannot be hooked, routes lead_in_span's noise floor through a seam, and maps f_mix None to Rational(0).
items.evidence: Ties were never observed in any probe. Refused (NotImplementedError): non-float32 or non-2-D CarrierStats.stat, non-1-D fe, non-2-D chunk table. Not hookable via acquire's module attributes: helpers inside native composites (_a2_input, _preamble_sums, CubicSpline, carrier_line_stats). lead_in_span's noise floor uses a NoisePsdFn seam. f_mix None -> Rational(0) for a hand-built _A2Input/_A2Channel; no real caller produces that.

items.what: A3 differs in a few places: TbdHit.f_hz and _path_line fit by QR instead of numpy's SVD polyfit, and inputs where Python errors or returns garbage raise NotImplementedError. f_hz is computed once per hit, eagerly for the first hit, and tbd_viterbi reads float32 E in place at half the memory.
items.evidence: f_hz intercept 1.6e-15, slope 3.6e-10 relative (ctest holds f_hz to 1e-9 Hz). NotImplementedError for a narrow band, B < |max_step| < 2B (with numpy's wording), and fe dtypes other than complex64/complex128/float64. shape_frames is reached through a TbdOptions::keep_fn seam. Every other TbdHit field is bit-exact and in the same order, except p_value (2.1e-16).

items.what: cwid refuses column-major 2-D unit stacks, complex64 channels, float32 noise_psd and rank > 2 stacks rather than compute different bits. match is bit-exact only where OpenBLAS dispatches the SkylakeX ddot.
items.evidence: numpy sums column-major stacks pairwise per column, differing from 8 rows up; row-major stacks in any stride pattern are exact. A 0-d input gives the reference's IndexError. Non-x86 BLAS ddot is allowed 1e-10 for match.

items.what: Hand-written ctest pins were wrong twice, each caught on the first ctest run. Every other pin was generated from Python by script and passed first time, so pins should never be typed.
items.evidence: np.polyfit([1.0],[1.0],1) assumed [1,1], but numpy's minimum-norm answer is [0.5, 0.5] (test_npstats.cpp 'one point, degree 1'). TINY n_sym assumed 1024, actually 1753 (test_ce_rx.cpp "sym has shape (3,), expected (1753,)"). Generator scripts: scratchpad pins.py, fe/pins.py, pins2.py, from infra_testgen splitmix counters.

items.what: A missing top-level meta key first surfaced as an IndexError from the C++ JSON accessor, which reads like a bug in the port rather than a malformed file. A dedicated pyjson::KeyError, mapped to Python's KeyError and read in Python's key order, makes the first missing key reported ('header') match Python.
items.evidence: native/core/qrss/pyjson.hpp KeyError; tests/test_qrss_native_types.py missing-key tests

items.what: The non-slow tier of the named --native-qrss=rx suites barely exercises the receiver. The per-module parity files and smoke/lunits/multipass carry the coverage, while test_qrss_receiver's real coverage is in a slow tier the agents were not allowed to run.
items.evidence: test_qrss_track.py 5 passed / 8 deselected; test_qrss_receiver.py 4 passed / 55 deselected (wave 4 skeleton review); 'test_qrss_receiver.py's non-slow tier is only 4 tests, so most of its coverage of this lane under --native-qrss=rx comes from the slow tier, which was not run' (wave 5 A1/A2 review)

items.what: The required 1/64 Hz noise-mask sweep is too slow for the default tier, so it is marked slow. The default tier sweeps at 1/4 Hz and a ctest pins a digest of the one-hertz masks.
items.evidence: 17,922 positions, about 60 s per band in Python; run once with 0 mismatches. The ctest digest (cd464fb6...) covers 282 one-hertz masks over both bands (99,138 flat bins). The frontend review did not rerun the slow sweep.

items.what: The worktree sandbox refused compound shell commands (cd plus a heredoc, $PWD, computed command names). The working pattern was to write scripts to the scratchpad with Write and run python on their absolute path.
items.evidence: several refusals in the frontend lane session; native/tests/qrss/test_*.cpp header comments carry the generating expressions

items.what: Several parity tolerances were looser than the plan's bar or than what was measured, and reviewers tightened them. A tolerance helper deserves the same adversarial reading as the code it checks.
items.evidence: Frontend: _fe_close skipped the '<=1e-5 of samples differ' count and exempted parts below 1e-3 of scale; _ch_close/_chan_same added atol 1e-6*max on top of rtol 1e-6 (tightened in commit 42005fa, all still pass). Wave 5 track timing: _carrier_lines was compared to a tolerance though exact, now bitwise. Wave 5 cwid: window tolerance allowed 0.1% of float32 values 1 ulp off against a measured 0, now 1e-4.

items.what: Several parity files ran near or over the ~40 s per-file budget, especially with agents sharing 4 CPUs. Timings were noisy for the same reason.
items.evidence: frontend ~35-40 s of a 46.5 s three-file run; track 31.9 s; track_timing 42.8 s, trimmed by cutting the paths probe from 24 to 16 trials; acquire_a12 34.6 s; cwid ~35 s and acquire_tbd ~36 s under shared load. 'normalise ... swinging with machine load' (wave 4 frontend).

items.what: Bitwise parity checks over signed zeros and ties, plus return-type checks, caught two bugs that the digests and the --native-qrss suites could not.
items.evidence: std::nth_element in median_filter's generic path returned -0.0 where scipy's NI_Select returns 0.0 (test_qrss_native_ndfilter.py::test_signed_zeros_and_ties); a1_gamma returned a Python float where acquire returns np.float64 (test_qrss_native_acquire_stats.py::test_scalars)

items.what: Per-function parity on C-contiguous random inputs missed the preamble_p layout bug. Running acquire's real callers with every row monkeypatched and diffing whole results found it on the first run, and wave 5 made this whole-caller A/B mandatory in every parity file.
items.evidence: test_acquire_end_to_end_on_the_cpp first failed at acquire[2].cell_lam (337.535874989212 vs 337.5358749892118) while the 35 existing parity tests passed. The wave 5 script COMMON requires 'WHOLE-CALLER A/B (required)' with that test as the pattern.

items.what: A natural-looking erasure fixture tested nothing: erase_s=((5,15),) on TINY lands entirely in the preamble/CW region, so every output equalled the unerased pass. The fixture moved to (25,35) s, and a test now asserts that each fixture has the property its label names. Guard the guard.
items.evidence: Erased positions 164-495; data starts at 661. tests/qrss_demod_tracks.py; tests/test_qrss_native_demod.py::test_the_tracks_cover_what_they_claim (>100 erased data symbols, header known/unknown, meas mask present).

items.what: The demod review found the numeric core bit-identical on every probe, and all eight real bugs were in the bindings: how and when arguments are read, and refusals. Reviews should probe argument forms and refusals, not only values.
items.evidence: tests/qrss_demod_probes.py and test_probe_* in the five parity files: 151 new tests, all passing only after review commits 7ff77c6 and 8e2c4d1 (266 tests, up from 115)

items.what: A pybind11 binding built a py::float_ inside a py::gil_scoped_release scope, crashing on one path only. Whole-caller tests missed it because the receiver never calls that path; keep the nogil block to the computation and build Python objects after it.
items.evidence: segfault only on _kf_forward store=False (native/bindings/module/qrss/track.cpp kf_forward_py), found by test_kalman, fixed in ff2f7ba by the port agent

items.what: Pinning a synthetic end-to-end track() pass in the ctest was cheap and strong. A CE TINY signal over exact-binary-fraction 'noise' reproduces the capture bit for bit in both languages, so q, meas and the decisions are pinned exactly; it also hosts a two-thread reentrancy check.
items.evidence: native/tests/qrss/test_track.cpp test_synthetic_pass (capture digest 134cbc75...)

items.what: For a long iterative routine the strongest check is a swap test: assign the C++ versions of the known non-bitwise leaves over the reference's, run the reference, and require bit-for-bit equality. It proves everything downstream is the reference's arithmetic and names each divergence seed; the same idea checked gate V's decision logic.
items.evidence: test_track_is_the_reference_up_to_smooth_and_templates. Swapping _smooth alone still left P 2.0e-5 on the lead-in call, which revealed SIMD exp in sf as a second seed. test_gate_v_composition: bitwise equality in all 8 scenarios.

items.what: Absolute tolerances on an ill-conditioned output are fixture luck. The original u/P bounds passed their two fixtures by a 12x margin and failed on the first drifting lead-in scenario probed; the conditional bit-for-bit check is what carries the claim.
items.evidence: test_track_on_the_receivers_calls held P at 1e-5; test_track_with_a_lead_in measured 2.0e-5 (bound 1e-4 plus the conditional check)

items.what: Spying on the reference made its internal intermediates checkable without copying its code into the test. The spy replaces the module's np with a proxy that records np.full's 2-D -inf grids and _segment_timing's calls.
items.evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_track_timing.py _NpSpy and _ref_fit (FFT grid, x, sig2 and peak inputs compared directly)

items.what: A whole-caller A/B that only compares results with the reference proves nothing if the rows silently never reach the C++. Each A/B must count calls into every native entry point, assert that each row target is the binding, and check that callers beyond receive_pass are reached; reviewers added this in every wave 5 lane.
items.evidence: A1/A2: call counters and target-is-binding assertions; preamble_search count >= 20 in the acquire A/B; without them both A/Bs would pass on pure Python. Track timing: receive_pass alone never reached receiver._gate's second verify_track or em.pass_path; the test now asserts verify == 2 + len(gates), verify_track == len(gates) + 2*len(refs), line_path == refine_path == len(refs). A3/cwid: spies prove track_before_detect, _hit_to_detection, frame_map, keying_type, window_soft, window_llr, read and match ran.

items.what: The brief's cwid A/B, receive_pass on CE TINY, would have been vacuous. TINY frames have no callsign windows, so cwid is never called; the A/B runs on SHORT and L_SHORT instead and is marked slow.
items.evidence: receiver._cw_result: `if spec.n_win == 0: return None, None`; slow receive_pass A/B ce-short 7.3 s, l-short 6.7 s

items.what: Claiming bit-exactness on a numpy reduction requires knowing which kernel numpy dispatches to at this version. einsum's optimize path, np.angle and float32 np.log all leave the C library, and two of the three were found only by bit-level probes, not by reading the Python.
items.evidence: scratchpad einprobe.py; test_numpys_float32_log

items.what: The receive-pass A/Bs compared Detection.uid exactly, but uid hashes the float32 z, so a 1e-13 Hz detection shift can flip it. The exact uid comparison was dropped, as cpp-port-plan 4.1 requires.
items.evidence: test_receive_pass_on_the_cpp edit (A1/A2 review); track core: 'A pass_uid's sha8 suffix may differ (it hashes float32 z)'

items.what: pybind11 without stl.h compiles fine but fails at runtime when a std::vector is passed to py::object.attr(...), such as reshape. Build shapes as py::tuple explicitly.
items.evidence: first parity run: 'Unable to convert call argument' on reshape; fixed with shape_tuple() in both binding files

items.what: A synthetic OOK callsign stub must key the carrier in the plain units too, not only in key-down units. Without it read_ml on the OOK stub reads garbage while the FSK test passes, which looks like a port bug.
items.evidence: Plain units are 0-4 and 184-191. scratchpad dbg_ook.py; the fixed stub reads K1ABC (gen_pins.py line 125).

items.what: Peak memory of one call inside a long-lived Python process can be measured without tracemalloc's overhead: write '5' to /proc/self/clear_refs to reset VmHWM, then read VmHWM after the call.
items.evidence: scratchpad time_full.py; used for the +202 MB vs +100 MB track_before_detect figures

items.what: Building a synthetic FULL capture is the slow part of any FULL-slot test. Cos/sin of exactly reduced turns plus a power-of-two FFT halved it, and the FULL-slot test stays slow-tier with the same sizes kept in the fast tier as matrices.
items.evidence: np.exp of a 7 M complex array plus an odd-length ifft took 13.6 s, against about 6 s for the reduced-turns version on this VM. Fast-tier test_full_size_pieces ~2 s; slow test_track_before_detect_full_slot 13 s.

items.what: Add tools/gen_qrss_rx_config.py --check to CI so a stale rx_config.hpp turns CI red.

items.evidence: Frontend shared_changes_needed. Done in commit 7245713: 'StreamFE's ALIGN and HALO now come from the generated rx_config.hpp'.

items.what: pyjson and pass_uid locale safety could not be tested under a comma decimal locale, because only C/POSIX locales are installed.
items.evidence: Skeleton review notes: pyjson parses through pynum::py_float and formats through frame::py_repr; pass_uid prints '%.0f'

items.what: In the transmit lane's ce.cpp, at_positions, phase_at, phase_grid and var_grid compute values for an L frame where the reference asserts, and phase_grid/var_grid spread a NaN or inf over fewer samples than scipy's upfirdn. The demod reviewer listed both, did not fix them, and ce.cpp was not touched afterwards.
items.evidence: NaN/inf spreads over 121 samples against 128 on tiny at 250 Hz because the C++ skips zero taps. Suggested fixes: move ce_rx::require_ce_layout into ce.cpp; run the zero taps or document it. Affects _mean_template_grid only with non-finite symbols, which EM never produces.

items.what: The math lane did not compare the x86_64 cross build. Agreement with scipy's special functions elsewhere holds only to that platform libm's ulp.
items.evidence: math lane parity 'Not compared' list

items.what: Add shared converters for CarrierStats, _A2Input, _A2Channel, PreambleHit, PreambleKind, TbdHit and Acquisition in rx_types.hpp and _rx.py. In wave 5 the A1/A2 and A3 bindings converted them locally.
items.evidence: A1/A2 and A3/cwid shared_changes_needed; done in wave 6a (commit 627657e '... shared acquisition converters')

items.what: preamble_p's gammaincc is now the largest single item in preamble_search and slower than scipy's. A faster regularized-gamma upper tail, or skipping it when Lambda is far from the threshold, is the next A2 performance lever.
items.evidence: ~26 ms per call in C++ against scipy's ~17.5 ms (A1/A2 port); special.cpp later gained only ndtri/norm_isf/gamma_logsf (wave 10)

items.what: _preamble_sums is slower than numpy's BLAS zgemm einsum. This is the place to vectorise or block if A2 becomes a cost on Android.
items.evidence: _preamble_sums CE py 0.0172 s vs C++ 0.0220 s, L 0.0079 vs 0.0131 (A1/A2 review)

items.what: Making lead_in_span's z bit-exact would need a scipy-style real-input FFT path in convolve.hpp for complex data with real taps. This is optional because the span is unaffected away from z == z_min.
items.evidence: A1/A2 review shared_changes_needed (optional); no later change to convolve.cpp

items.what: cwid::unit_source depends on track::TrackResult and track::NoisePsdFn from trackbase.hpp, and its signature was to be re-checked after the track lane merged. No source in this scope records the check.
items.evidence: A3/cwid port shared_changes_needed

items.what: An in-place cfar_normalise variant in acquire_stats would let tbd_emissions skip one frames x bins float32 copy, about 34 MB on FULL.
items.evidence: A3/cwid port shared_changes_needed (optional)

items.what: Correct the track.hpp header comment and the tests/qrss_native/track.py docstring, which still said the timing functions were to come; they live in track_timing.
items.evidence: Track timing shared_changes_needed. Done in commit 21ba9bf: 'track.hpp and the track rows file said the timing functions were still to come; they are track_timing's'.

items.what: Neither implementation's tests reach refine_timing's 3-D gamma Newton branch, so the port of that branch is checked only by evaluation, never by a taken path.
items.evidence: track core review 'Not compared: an injected or simulated timing that actually takes refine_timing's 3-D gamma branch'

items.what: Three minor A3/cwid residues were left as is: tbd_viterbi uses `long` for bin indices, which is 32-bit on MSVC; TbdHit.f_hz is computed eagerly for the first hit; and the f_mix None -> Rational(0) mapping in the A1/A2 binding remains.
items.evidence: Harmless because B is at most about 10^4 bins. Only the point where a polyfit error would be raised could differ. All three are recorded unfixed in the A3/cwid and A1/A2 reviews.

items.what: math::TypeError derived from std::invalid_argument, so the C++ spelling of `except ValueError`, such as PathFn's spline fallback, also caught TypeErrors that Python lets propagate. It now derives from std::logic_error.
items.evidence: native/core/math/errors.hpp; a ctest pins that it is not an invalid_argument (test_npstats.cpp test_average)

items.what: lstsq's LAPACK fallback for rcond <= 0 or >= 1 used DBL_EPSILON (2^-52), but dgelsd/dlalsd use DLAMCH('Epsilon') = 2^-53, which changes the rank for a singular value between 1.11e-16 and 2.22e-16 of the largest.
items.evidence: diag(1, 1.5e-16), rcond=-1: numpy rank 2, port rank 1; native/core/math/linalg.cpp:260; tests/test_qrss_native_math.py::test_lstsq_edges

items.what: BSpline::derivative's errstate emulation raised 'not differentiable' for inf/0, where scipy's splder returns +-inf. Under IEEE, inf/0 is an exact inf and raises no flag; only finite-nonzero/0 raises divide-by-zero, and inf-inf or 0/0 raise invalid.
items.evidence: native/core/math/bspline.cpp:183-191; parity cases in test_bspline_eval_and_derivative (inf/0 in both positions, NaN, zero numerator, inf-inf)

items.what: pass_uid threw OverflowError for a millihertz count past int64, with a message built by locale-dependent std::to_string(double), where Python's round() is unbounded. It is now exact, with Python's own NaN/inf errors.
items.evidence: ctest and parity cover 1e17, 1e300, -1e300 and +-2^63/1000

items.what: The skeleton's contract lacked np.average(weights=) although three later lanes needed it, and test_pathfn_refusals skipped checking the OverflowError text on the false claim that the C++ text names int64.
items.evidence: Both sides say 'cannot convert float infinity to integer'; math::average was added with a binding, a ctest and a parity test (skeleton review)

items.what: npz.cpp, from an earlier wave, opened files with std::ifstream/ofstream from a narrow UTF-8 std::string. MSVC reads that in the ANSI code page, so non-ASCII paths break on Windows, and PassResult save/load inherited it.
items.evidence: Example: a user profile like C:\Users\José. Reported unfixed in the skeleton review's shared_changes_needed. Fixed in wave 7 (commit a31240f 'UTF-8 paths through one file helper').

items.what: chan.cpp counted a NaN sample as signal in the noise table's padding fraction, where Python's np.abs(ch) > 0 is false for NaN. This changed the good-window set and the noise floor on captures with NaN.
items.evidence: old C++ gave 2.0 where Python gives 3.5 (test_padding_fraction_counts_nan_as_the_reference_does); native/core/qrss/chan.cpp:147

items.what: StreamFE::push erased the consumed prefix once per block, so one long push was quadratic, and the gap grows with recording length. Live chunks are small, which is why existing tests never showed it; it now consumes from an offset.
items.evidence: A 900 s WAV replay pushed whole (7.2M samples, 900 blocks of 8000): 2.85 s in C++ vs Python 0.90 s before, 0.45 s after (Python 0.90-1.03 s). Same output, with 2 of 3.6M samples 1 ulp apart. Commit 1a52e50.

items.what: preamble_scales/preamble_p were bit-exact only for a C-ordered S. On the real call path _preamble_sums yields a Fortran-ordered S that numpy sums one term at a time, so Lambda and p differed in the last bit and the difference reached PreambleHit.cell_lam.
items.evidence: Up to 42% of cells differed. Fixed with aq::SumOrder plus a numpy layout probe in the binding; pinned by test_preamble_p_follows_numpys_layout and a sequential-order ctest digest.

items.what: spectrogram windowed complex input as (re*w, im*w) instead of numpy's complex product with w+0j, so a non-finite sample gave inf frames where numpy gives NaN frames. Real input also lacked its own overload.
items.evidence: Probe: C++ had 1825 inf cells where Python had 0, for complex64 and complex128; pinned in test_spectrogram_nonfinite_samples_and_real_dtypes and the ctest

items.what: Three integer UBs in acquire_stats: st + k could overflow int64 in spectrogram, py_round cast NaN/inf/out-of-range values to int64 where Python raises round()'s ValueError/OverflowError, and a1_gamma's M*M overflowed for M > 3037000499.
items.evidence: py_round is used by frame_len, band_cov and a1_gamma; the ctest pins a1_gamma(3037000500) and round()'s errors (math review commits 9c3d2d5, f906ef0)

items.what: band_cov's cache keyed on a NaN fs returned another fs's tables, because NaN is equivalent to every std::map key under operator<. It now validates fs before the lookup; validate a float before using it as a cache key.
items.evidence: pinned by the ctest 'band_cov(5, NaN) with a table cached' and test_non_finite_fs_is_rounds_error

items.what: The acquire_stats bindings mishandled several argument forms: refusal texts and check order differed from the reference, values were wrapped or read with the wrong truthiness, and the spectrogram binding ignored chunk.
items.evidence: spectral_shape with a negative local_bins used its own text instead of numpy's 'negative dimensions are not allowed'; local_bins past int's range wrapped; a true value whose int() is 0 (0.5) read as false. The spectrogram binding ignored chunk (Python raises for 0), checked len(bins) through numpy, used the wrong 0-d starts text, and checked starts before bins.

items.what: The matched filter bindings (CE and L) handled argument forms wrongly. A float n0 was truncated by int() instead of raising IndexError, a 0-d pos returned values instead of TypeError, n0 and z were validated even when the loop never runs, and a 2-D pos was flattened.
items.evidence: n0 = 1.5 gave values shifted by half a sample; the reference raises 'arrays used as indices must be of integer (or boolean) type' (demod review commit 7ff77c6, mf_rx.hpp)

items.what: ce_rx mean_template and _mean_template_grid given an L FrameSpec laid the frame out as L and returned values, where the reference raises frame.layout's AssertionError.
items.evidence: "1237 header slots for 2474 bits", or "512 data slots for 1024 latents" for l-tiny; fixed with ce_rx::require_ce_layout

items.what: For L tracks the demod binding flattened 2-D hdr_bits, pushed non-0/1 values through a uint8 cast, and treated an empty meas array as None. Each of these silently gave different numbers where the reference raises.
items.evidence: -1 became 255; 0.5 and NaN became 0. An empty meas raises IndexError in the reference via np.asarray(meas, bool)[gi]. Fixed with demod_rx::hdr_bits_of and TrackView::meas_given.

items.what: CE calibrate read a stub without tr.c, or with c None or a list, as an empty template and failed with IndexError where the reference raises AttributeError/TypeError. extract(calibrate_kappa=False) also read tr.c, which the reference never does.
items.evidence: demod review commit 8e2c4d1

items.what: The track ctest used M_PI, which MSVC defines only under _USE_MATH_DEFINES, so the Windows build would not compile; it now uses std::numbers::pi. Its two-thread check also ran after the capture's NoisePsdSlot was filled, so the lazy-fill race was never exercised.
items.evidence: std::numbers::pi is bit-identical to np.pi, so the pinned digest holds; the check now races on a fresh capture and requires identical N and a filled slot (track core review commit 8bb2508)

items.what: The track parity test's docstring blamed np.convolve's BLAS sum alone for the u/P departure from Python. On a drifting lead-in pass numpy's SIMD exp in sf also seeds it, giving P 2.0e-5, above the test's 1e-5 bound.
items.evidence: swap test added pinning both seeds (track core review)

items.what: lead_in_span computed |sum(m[w])| with the np.abs ufunc formula, but the reference applies Python's builtin abs (libm hypot) to the np.sum scalar. The two differ by 1 ulp in about 21% of windows, which could flip the span at z == z_min; this was the one real C++ bug in the A1/A2 lane.
items.evidence: changed to std::hypot in native/core/qrss/acquire_a12.cpp lead_in_impl (review commit 3a4efca)

items.what: The cwid binding summed every 2-D unit stack row by row after a C-order copy. For a column-major stack numpy sums pairwise per column, so _combine/read_ml/read/match gave different bits from 8 rows up; such stacks are now refused.
items.evidence: No caller makes such a stack; row-major layouts including reversed, strided and broadcast are exact (A3/cwid review commit 8feef3e)

items.what: A cwid test comment claimed match was measured at 4.6e-16 when it is bit-exact. The track timing tests also lacked a q-floor scenario and randomised edge probes; these were added, and no C++ bug was found in track_timing.
items.evidence: match 0 difference over 5000 draws; the q-floor probe is TINY at -15 dB (test_probe_steady_weak_q_floor); 16 random fit_timing trials, 16 path captures, 14 _segment_timing trials

items.what: drop_symbol_rate_aliases requires an alias's timing to be within T/2 (15.2 ms). On a 0 dB CE signal hinted at f-1/T, a passed alias 19.4 ms off was kept, so the acquisition reported two CE preamble hits for one signal (the +1/T alias, 12.6 ms off, was dropped). This shows only when a hint or an A1 line lands on the alias; gate V then has to reject it.

An L hint within 2.5 Hz of a failed L hit at an A1 line reuses that hit (near[0]) and is never searched at the hint itself, so a hint's outcome depends on unrelated A1 lines. Probably intended. The reviewer adds that h.passed is always False on that branch, so the lookup only saves one A2 search.
items.evidence: probe_band.py on TL._capture(l-short, 1203.4, 0 dB, seed 10): a hint at the -1/T_L alias 1186.9 Hz (A1 line at 1184.95 Hz) is never searched there. A hint at 1188.0 reaches it, and it passes A2-L with p about 1e-22.
